The pricing decision

The supplied CMA supports conventional asking and achieved rents in the $2,500–$2,750 range for closely matched homes. It does not demonstrate a 21-day result: all four leased comparables report 35–66 cumulative days on market. The owner-confirmed prior lease at $2,450 provides a property-specific reason to start at that same rent. It is $50 below the closest $2,500 alternatives, but it is a starting strategy rather than evidence that a 21-day lease is assured.

Recommendation: start at $2,450 base rent; reduce to $2,395 promptly if qualified demand is insufficient.
At $2,450, annual scheduled base rent is $29,400. This starting rent matches the home’s prior lease and is $50 below the closest active same-size competitor.

The 21-day goal means a signed lease, not necessarily tenant occupancy within 21 days. Timing depends on condition, access, qualified demand and approval turnaround; it is not guaranteed.

Adjust for the home—not just the headline rent

DifferenceAdjustment to comparable rentReasoning
Same 1,620 sq. ft.$0Six comparables match the subject’s size.
1,652 versus 1,620 sq. ft.About −$16/mo32 sq. ft. × $0.50 marginal monthly rent per sq. ft.; only a 2% size difference.
Confirmed corner versus interior−$50 to −$100/moAdditional side exposure, light and lot setting; applies to 14187 and 14404.
Washer/dryer versus hookups only−$25 to −$50/moAppliance convenience; use only if the subject still lacks both machines.
Meaningfully upgraded finishes−$25 to −$75/moApply only where the comparable’s documented finish package exceeds the subject’s.
Shared gate, amenities, courtyard, garage$0 for like-for-like featuresNo automatic premium for benefits already common to the comparison set.
Different utilities / servicesActual verified monthly valueEqualize water, internet, grounds and mandatory fees before comparing total tenant cost.

These are underwriting judgments, not statistically isolated or appraisal-derived adjustments. Do not multiply a small size difference by the full average rent per sq. ft.: rent also buys bedrooms, garage and community access. No automatic one-year age adjustment is applied to these 2021–2023 homes. Avoid stacking overlapping finish and condition adjustments.

The strongest price bridge

14363 Sapelo leased at $2,500 with the same 1,620 sq. ft., a courtyard and a two-car garage described in remarks. If the subject still has hookups only, a $25–$50 laundry adjustment suggests $2,450–$2,475 before a speed discount. Starting at $2,450 sits at the low end of that illustrative equivalent and matches the subject’s owner-confirmed prior lease. It also places base rent $50 below the closest active asking rent. A reduction to $2,395 would create a more visible value advantage if the initial response is weak.

14315 Sapelo asks $2,500 and advertises quartz counters, upgraded living-area flooring and EV charging. A conservative $50–$100 combined feature allowance, if the subject lacks those upgrades, indicates $2,400–$2,450. This is an asking-price comparison, not proof of achieved value, but it supports $2,450 as a defensible starting point near the top of that illustrative range, with $2,395 available as the next step if qualified renters do not respond.

Vacancy is the silent tax

A higher rent helps only if the additional income exceeds the vacancy it creates. This illustration assumes a home ready and vacant at launch, no concessions and an immediate rent start once leased; actual move-in dates can change the outcome.

Illustrative scenarioVacancy within 365 daysGross rent collected*Effective monthly rent*
$2,450 leased / rent starts on day 2121 days$27,708$2,309
$2,500 leased / rent starts on day 3535 days$27,123$2,260
$2,500 leased / rent starts on day 4343 days$26,466$2,205
$2,700 leased / rent starts on day 4646 days$28,317$2,360

*Gross base-rent illustration over the first 365 days from launch: monthly rent × 12 × (365 − vacant days) ÷ 365; effective monthly = gross ÷ 12. Rounded to the nearest dollar. Excludes fees, turnover costs, concessions and operating expenses. These are scenarios, not forecasts; comparable CDOM is not substituted for actual vacancy. A $2,500 strategy has only about 6.9 extra vacant days beyond a day-21 start to match $2,450. The annual scheduled difference between $2,450 and $2,395 is $660; about 8.2 vacant days at $2,450 consume that amount. Higher rent can still win if genuinely attainable, but is less aligned with the requested speed goal.

A 21-day leasing plan

Before day 1Confirm appliances and included services. Deliver a clean courtyard, fresh presentation, accurate photos and straightforward showing access.
Days 1–7Launch at $2,450. Respond the same business day; track qualified inquiries, completed showings, applications and specific objections.
Days 7–10If there are no qualified applications and weak showing conversion, correct presentation/access issues promptly and reduce to $2,395 with owner approval. The 21-day target favors an early adjustment over waiting for the listing to age.
Days 14–21If still unleased, reassess current competing inventory and renter feedback immediately; consider $2,350 if $2,395 has not generated qualified applications, subject to owner approval. Do not wait until day 21 to react or relax screening standards.

Offer a straightforward 12-month term and disclose required recurring charges. Confirm whether qualified pets can be considered under owner and HOA rules; do not assume a pet policy. Keep Verandah’s established resident-selection standards throughout.

Why start at the prior $2,450 rent?

Verandah confirms that the home last leased at $2,450 per month. That actual property-specific outcome is more relevant than simply targeting the higher neighborhood average. Starting at the same rent recognizes the home’s prior acceptance while positioning it $50 below the closest active same-size competitor.

However, the current $2,500 competitor has already been available for 21 days, and the four leased comparables took 35–66 days. The previous lease does not guarantee the same demand today. If the first 7–10 days do not produce qualified applications, we recommend a prompt reduction to $2,395. A further move to $2,350 may be necessary if demand remains weak. All reductions require owner approval; resident-selection standards remain unchanged.

Public price histories show the subject’s 2025 advertising stepping down from $2,850 to $2,450 before removal. Those advertised reductions are historical context only; the prior achieved rent is confirmed by Verandah.
